version.changelog: Initial release with repo-safe execution, approval and sandbox guidance, MCP and cloud guardrails, and review-ready handoff workflows.

llm.summary: This skill is a safety-oriented guide for using Codex, and its sensitive behaviors are disclosed, bounded, and tied to that purpose.

dimensions.detail: The skill discusses high-impact Codex modes such as workspace writes, full access, MCP, cloud apply, app-server, and local providers, but frames them as explicit trust-boundary decisions rather than defaults.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown guidance only, no executable scripts, dependency installers, hooks, or automatic runtime payloads.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions repeatedly require preflight checks, explicit user approval for dangerous bypass, remote MCP, cloud apply, production commands, and irreversible side effects.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It proposes durable operating notes under ~/codex/ and references local Codex config state, but setup instructions require user permission before creating memory files and say not to scrape secrets.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is to operate Codex safely for repo-aware coding, reviews, MCP, cloud, sandboxing, and handoffs; the inspected files consistently support that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you want Codex workflow guidance and are comfortable with Codex sending selected prompts, repository context, and tool results to OpenAI during actual Codex runs. Treat MCP, cloud apply, app-server, full-access sandbox, and persistent ~/codex/ notes as opt-in choices that should stay under your explicit control.
llm.findings:
[AS1] expected: The references to ~/.codex/config.toml are disclosed as Codex configuration context and local state; the artifact does not instruct scraping credentials and explicitly says not to scrape tokens from arbitrary files.
[EA5] expected: The codex exec, sandbox, dangerous bypass, cloud, app-server, and local-provider examples are expected for a Codex operations skill and are surrounded by warnings, approval requirements, and least-privilege guidance.
[E2] expected: The OPENAI_API_KEY command reads a single named environment variable for an intentional API-key login flow, not bulk environment harvesting or exfiltration.
[P2] expected: The HTML comments in memory-template.md are visible template placeholders describing what the user may record; they do not contain hidden unauthorized directives.
[AS2] expected: The MCP guidance tells the user to inspect/list configured servers to reduce scope creep and remove unnecessary servers; this is coherent with MCP safety review, not covert config abuse.
